title: Optically Resolved Excited State Hyperfine Structure of a Silicon Colour Centre in the Telecom Bands
authors: Austin Woolverton, Nicholas Brunelle, Mehdi Keshavarz, Laurent Bergeron, Evan R. MacQuarrie, Yehudah Ackermann, Melanie Gascoine, Nikolay V. Abrosimov, Stephanie Simmons, Daniel Higginbottom, Michael Thewalt
abstract: Nuclear spin qubits in silicon offer exceptionally coherent quantum memory, and optically-interfaced spins are a promising platform for both quantum networking and distributed quantum computing. It has been proposed that emitters with diamagnetic ground states may permit an optical interface to nuclear spin memories via metastable, hyperfine-coupled excited states while suppressing key sources of decoherence. Until now, direct optical observation of suitable transitions in silicon colour centres has remained elusive. Here we characterize the singly-ionized interstitial aluminum donor (Al$_\mathrm{i}^+$) in isotopically purified $^{28}$Si and find several novel features of this little-studied defect. We measure bright emission and strong optical transitions and, in contrast to previous studies of this centre, attribute its emission to an exchange-split spin triplet and singlet level of the lowest-energy 1s:T$_2$ excited state. We measure the excited-state lifetimes and, as a consequence of its narrow emission linewidth, observe the fine and hyperfine structure of the long-lived triplet state. This constitutes the first measurement of an optically-resolved hyperfine structure in the excited state of a telecommunications-band silicon colour centre.
summary: The research characterizes the $	ext{Al}_i^+$ defect in silicon, aiming to use its excited state as an interface for nuclear spin qubits. By performing high-resolution magnetospectroscopy, the authors report resolving both fine and hyperfine structure in the excited state. This breakthrough confirms that this silicon center can function as a viable spin-photon interface for quantum information processing.
main_problem: The primary goal was to optically observe and characterize the hyperfine structure of an excited state within a silicon color center ($	ext{Al}_i^+$) operating in the telecom band.
main_result: The authors successfully measured the first optically-resolved hyperfine structure in the excited state of this silicon defect, confirming its potential as a spin-photon interface for quantum memory applications.
method: The study employed low-temperature optical spectroscopy (PL and absorption) combined with magnetospectroscopy to resolve fine and hyperfine splittings.
model_or_system: The system is the singly-ionized interstitial aluminum donor ($	ext{Al}_i^+$) in $^{28}	ext{Si}$. The electronic states are modeled using an exchange interaction, leading to singlet and triplet excited levels coupled by Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC).
key_observables: Zero-phonon emission spectrum, excited-state lifetimes ($	au_s \approx 1.8\ \mu	ext{s}$, $	au_t \approx 25.5\ 	ext{ms}$), and resolved hyperfine transition frequencies.
important_parameters: The energy splitting between singlet and triplet states ($\Delta E_{st} \approx 21.3\ 	ext{meV}$) and the isotropic contact hyperfine coupling parameter ($a_{	ext{iso}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on modeling the electronic structure using effective Hamiltonians incorporating SOC, Zeeman effects, and nuclear spin coupling terms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the proposed level structures (showing $J$ splitting) and the measured PL spectra at various temperatures and magnetic fields, revealing distinct zero-phonon emission features.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical platform ($	ext{Al}_i^+$ in $^{28}	ext{Si}$) to detailing spectroscopic measurements (PL/absorption), modeling the electronic structure using SOC and exchange interactions, and finally resolving both fine and hyperfine structures through detailed spectral analysis.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the development of solid-state quantum memories by demonstrating optical control over spin states in a highly coherent platform suitable for quantum networking applications.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Proposed level structure of Al+ i and PL excitation scheme. Each excited state includes an electron in the 1s:A1 ground level, and the 1s:T2 state splits under the exchange interaction. An emergent SOC separates the triplet state into effective J levels with degeneracy further lifted by the Zeeman interaction. The energy seperations are not to scale. The ISC allows for preferential population into the J = 1 triplet level. Optical excitation to 2p0, 2p±, and above-band (red) excitation, used for our PL measurements, are followed by rapid decay to the 1s:T2 manifold. Luminescence is observed from 1s:1T2 and 1s:3T2 (blue).

FIG. 2: (Blue) Photoluminescence spectrum of Al+ i at 4.2 K under resonant excitation of 2p±. The amplitude of the ZPL has been normalized to unity and truncated. The phonon side-band is compared to the silicon density of states (black) [47]. We indicate the transverse optical (TO), transverse acoustic (TA), longitudinal optical (LO), and longitudinal acoustic (LA) phonon modes at high symmetry points within the first Brillouin zone [22].

FIG. 3: PL spectra of 1s:3T2 at 4.2 K under above-band excitation and applied magnetic field, with ˆB ≈[110]. Each dot represents an extracted peak position. The eigenenergies of each sublevel within J = 0, 1, and 2 are determined from the exact solutions of the Hamiltonian (SM Section S2 [46]) and shown as solid, dashed, and dotted lines.

FIG. 4: The optically resolved hyperfine structure within the 1s:3T2(J = 1) ⇒1s:1A1 transition is shown for 0 mT (bottom) and 110 mT (top) with a fit to the electronic spin Hamiltonian and isotropic hyperfine (grey). Each PL spectrum was measured at 4.2 K using a resonant laser tuned to the 1s:1A1 ⇒2p± transition. The peak positions, shown as grey dots, are determined from a least-squares fit to multiple Gaussian-Lorentzian products with a shared background. The uncertainties of the transition energies are within the marker size.
